facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against a limited-readiness view is that the statements, debt notes and liquidity table cover every reported period through the third quarter of 2026. It weakens because USD 1,226.7 million of the USD 1,256.5 million of available credit sits on revolving lines whose availability depends on borrowing-base calculations that change monthly, so the covenant and borrowing-base terms decide how much of the reported funds can be used. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against reading the full-perimeter leverage as a creditor risk is asset matching: inventory of USD 6,624.3 million stands against floor plan notes of USD 6,566.8 million, and net finance receivables of USD 5,578.6 million against financing-operations debt of USD 4,509.2 million, so most of the added debt is backed by assets that turn over or amortise. That case would lose if used vehicle values or credit performance weakened, because the notes would then fall due faster than the assets convert; net credit losses on managed receivables were USD 47.8 million in the nine months to September 2026 against USD 54.1 million a year earlier, so that sign is absent today, and a reversal would be the first signal. A fuller maturity schedule for the revolvers, warehouse and non-recourse lines would show whether that matching holds in time as well as in amount. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Lithia sells new and used vehicles through franchised stores in the United States, the United Kingdom and Canada, and earns most of its profit from service, parts and finance and insurance. New vehicles are 49.70% of 2025 revenue but 20.39% of gross profit, while aftersales and finance and insurance together are 66.82% of gross profit, and the nine months to September 2026 show the same shape at 67.52%. That mix means vehicle margin compression, which cut new-vehicle gross profit per unit from USD 2,943 to USD 2,699 in the nine months, is cushioned by a service and finance base that is less tied to new-vehicle cycles. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Growth has come through purchases of stores funded by floor plan debt. facts.text: Earnings are stabilising but not yet growing. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against a weakening view is that the company's own leverage is flat since March 2026 at 3.07x, that the high point of 3.17x in June 2026 has already eased, that third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA rose 1.26% on the year, that net credit losses on managed receivables fell to USD 47.8 million in the nine months from USD 54.1 million, and that 95.24% of the added receivables and most floor plan debt is matched by assets. That case would win if trailing Adjusted EBITDA turned up toward the USD 1,701.9 million of a year ago while repurchases slowed to within operating cash flow. It would lose if used-vehicle values or borrowing-base availability fell, because the matched debt would then be repaid faster than the assets convert, or if the executed credit agreement shows distribution limits that are already close to binding. On governance, the company kept a lead independent director when the chief executive became chairman, which is a partial check on the combined role. ## Request

Lithia Motors Inc (issuer lad-1023128), as of 2026-11-18, credit_snapshot pathway: source readiness of the eight supplied filings and earnings releases for the financial foundation, business and governance, and fundamental credit modules. Scope is the effective source set through the third quarter of 2026; the run context supplies no legal documents, ratings, quotes, peers or portfolio.

## Findings
### Bottom line

The eight supplied filings and releases support the financial foundation, business profile and credit view through the third quarter of 2026, but creditors cannot test covenant headroom, guarantors or ratings from them.

The latest statements cover the nine months to 30 September 2026 and were signed 21 days before the cutoff. The 2025 annual report revised the 2024 comparatives, so 2024 figures should come from the 2025 report. Adjusted EBITDA appears only in the three 2026 earnings releases, and nothing dated after 28 October 2026 was supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 90; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_a2026q3exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation CALC-6
### Key findings

The set holds the annual reports for 2024 and 2025, the quarterly reports for the first three quarters of 2026 and an earnings release for each of those quarters, so every 2026 quarter has a filed report and a company release to cross-check.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_lad-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-03-31_lad-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-06-30_lad-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-04-29_a2026q1exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_a2026q2exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_a2026q3exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1

The 2025 annual report corrects an immaterial 2024 error in interest and fee income, lowering 2024 net income by USD 5.3 million to USD 816.3 million from USD 821.6 million, while the 2024 annual report still shows the older figure; the 2025 report governs for 2024, and the 2024 report remains the source for the 2023 balance sheet.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-K_2024-12-31_lad-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 77; calculation CALC-1

Cash flows are printed year to date only and no stand-alone fourth quarter of 2025 is printed, so quarterly figures have to be differenced; the supplied reports carry every input, for example fourth-quarter 2025 revenue of USD 9,197.8 million from full-year USD 37,634.9 million less nine-month USD 28,437.1 million.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; calculation CALC-2

Reported total debt of USD 16,256.3 million at 30 September 2026 equals the balance-sheet floor plan, term debt and securitisation notes, while the 2025 annual report's long-term debt note totals USD 9,840.8 million and leaves out floor plan notes, so the two totals are not comparable without a bridge.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-4

Balance-sheet cash of USD 374.0 million includes USD 265.9 million of restricted collections and customer deposits, so unrestricted cash is USD 108.1 million and the immediately available funds the company reports are USD 1,440.7 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; calculation CALC-5

Adjusted EBITDA and the net debt ratio are printed only in the three 2026 earnings releases, each with prior-year comparatives, so leverage at the 2025 year end is not printed in any supplied document.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-29_a2026q1exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 9; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_a2026q2exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_a2026q3exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11

No credit agreement, note indenture, rating report or proxy statement was supplied, so covenant levels, guarantor identities, collateral by instrument, ratings, directors and ownership are not established. The exhibit index lists a loan agreement with six amendments and four note indentures that name guarantors, and the annual report names the covenant types and a cross-default clause without levels and says the company monitors its credit ratings without printing one.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against a limited-readiness view is that the statements, debt notes and liquidity table cover every reported period through the third quarter of 2026. It weakens because USD 1,226.7 million of the USD 1,256.5 million of available credit sits on revolving lines whose availability depends on borrowing-base calculations that change monthly, so the covenant and borrowing-base terms decide how much of the reported funds can be used. Receipt of the credit agreement and the note indentures would make covenant headroom testable and would lift that limit; a further revision of reported figures beyond the 2024 correction would lower trust in the statements.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 46; calculation CALC-7
### Limitations
Readiness verdicts describe document coverage and definitions only; they do not test whether the printed figures are correct.
The 2026 quarterly statements and the earnings releases are unaudited, and the releases rank below the filings where they differ.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_a2026q3exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 6

## Findings
### Bottom line

Lithia carries 7.77x total debt to trailing reported EBITDA on its full balance sheet but 3.07x on the company's narrower measure, so creditor exposure depends on how much floor plan and finance-arm funding is treated as matched by assets.

On the full perimeter, leverage rose from 5.24x at the end of 2023 to 7.14x at the end of 2025 while cash interest cover fell from 4.05x to 2.93x, and trailing cover is 2.79x. About 74.5% of the debt added since 2023 is floor plan and securitisation notes, which finance inventory and finance receivables, and reported operating cash flow turned negative in the nine months to September 2026.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 74–75; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_a2026q3exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation CALC-27; calculation CALC-28
### Key findings

On all balance-sheet debt, total debt to reported EBITDA rose from 5.24x in 2023 to 6.48x in 2024, 7.14x in 2025 and 7.77x over the twelve months to 30 September 2026, and net of unrestricted cash from 4.84x to 7.71x. Total debt grew by USD 5,355.8 million over that span to USD 16,256.3 million while reported EBITDA moved only from USD 2,080.7 million to USD 2,093.4 million, so the ratio rose because debt grew, not because earnings fell; USD 2,931.3 million of the increase is floor plan notes and USD 1,060.1 million is non-recourse notes, together 74.5%.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_lad-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 74–75; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-4; calculation CALC-14; calculation CALC-24; calculation CALC-25; calculation CALC-26; calculation CALC-27

The company's own measure is 3.07x: net debt of USD 4,992.2 million over trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,627.2 million. It leaves out USD 6,570.3 million of inventory-related debt and USD 4,509.2 million of financing-operations debt and takes floor plan and financing interest out of EBITDA, so it measures the corporate layer, which is USD 5,176.8 million of debt before cash. A creditor to the corporate layer should read both figures: the full-perimeter ratio shows how much debt sits on the balance sheet, and the company's ratio shows what is left once asset-matched funding is set aside.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-21_a2026q3exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; calculation CALC-28; calculation CALC-36

Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 4.05x in 2023, 2.77x in 2024, 2.93x in 2025 and 2.79x over the trailing twelve months, while trailing cash interest of USD 750.4 million compares with USD 514.3 million in 2023. Floor plan interest and financing-operations interest are inside that cash interest, so cover on this perimeter is lower than the burden the corporate layer alone carries.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation CALC-15

Reported operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 204.9 million in the nine months to September 2026 against an inflow of USD 233.0 million a year earlier, because USD 831.4 million went into finance receivables and USD 555.0 million into inventory. The company's adjusted operating cash flow of USD 2,125.2 million adds back that finance receivables outflow and net floor plan borrowings of USD 1,542.2 million; USD 1,138.3 million of those borrowings came from converting inventory-secured revolvers into floor plan facilities, which changes where debt is recorded and earns no cash. After capex of USD 252.3 million, free cash flow was an outflow of USD 457.2 million, while shareholder returns of USD 665.6 million were paid and net financing inflow was USD 722.3 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; calculation CALC-29; calculation CALC-30

Immediately available funds were USD 1,440.7 million at 30 September 2026, made of USD 108.1 million unrestricted cash, USD 76.1 million of marketable securities and USD 1,256.5 million of available credit, and available credit fell from USD 1,359.2 million at the end of 2025. The principal schedule at the end of 2025 shows USD 71.6 million due in 2026 and USD 536.5 million in 2027, which includes the USD 400.0 million of 2027 senior notes, but it leaves out revolvers, warehouse facilities, non-recourse notes and floor plan notes, so the full near-term maturity wall is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 103; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99; calculation CALC-31; calculation CALC-34

The 2025 annual report revised 2024 for an immaterial error in interest and fee income, so 2024 is shown as revised, with net income of USD 816.3 million and not the USD 821.6 million first reported. Deferred revenue, which funds operations without interest, rose from USD 264.1 million at the end of 2023 to USD 499.4 million at September 2026, and contract liabilities on aftersales and lease vehicles were USD 549.7 million and USD 155.2 million; these are service obligations that unwind through delivery and sit outside debt.

Two events after the balance sheet are not in any period figure: an October 2026 acquisition of four stores and a dividend of USD 0.75 per share expected on 20 November 2026. The sources state neither the purchase price nor the total dividend, so no pro forma net debt is stated.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-21_a2026q3exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against reading the full-perimeter leverage as a creditor risk is asset matching: inventory of USD 6,624.3 million stands against floor plan notes of USD 6,566.8 million, and net finance receivables of USD 5,578.6 million against financing-operations debt of USD 4,509.2 million, so most of the added debt is backed by assets that turn over or amortise. That case would lose if used vehicle values or credit performance weakened, because the notes would then fall due faster than the assets convert; net credit losses on managed receivables were USD 47.8 million in the nine months to September 2026 against USD 54.1 million a year earlier, so that sign is absent today, and a reversal would be the first signal. A fuller maturity schedule for the revolvers, warehouse and non-recourse lines would show whether that matching holds in time as well as in amount.
### Limitations

Fiscal-year EBITDA is calculated by the issuer's own definition from statement lines, because the issuer states EBITDA only for 2025 and 2026 interim periods; trailing figures add the nine-month stubs.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-21_a2026q3exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75; calculation CALC-9; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-11

Debt is stated at balance-sheet carrying value, and instrument-level carrying values, security, ranking and guarantors are not disclosed in any supplied document, so no debt stack by seniority can be drawn.
Interim cash flow statements are year to date only and the interim statements are unaudited, so quarterly flows and the trailing ratios rest on differences of reported totals.

## Gaps

Adjusted EBITDA is not stated for 2023, 2024 or 2025 as a year, only for quarters, nine-month periods and trailing twelve months, so the adjusted ratios for those years are not calculable; severity is medium, and a fourth-quarter 2025 release or a house-adjusted measure would close it.

The legal rank, collateral and guarantors of every debt instrument are not stated in any supplied document, so no facility is drawn in the debt stack by seniority and the senior notes, bank facilities, non-recourse notes and mortgages are all left out of it; severity is high, and the executed credit agreement and note indentures would close it.

Instrument-level carrying values are not disclosed, only the aggregate unamortized issuance costs, so debt by instrument is shown at outstanding principal with one financing cost adjustment row; severity is low.

The scheduled principal table at 31 December 2025 leaves out revolving lines of credit, warehouse facilities, non-recourse notes and floor plan notes, and no later schedule is supplied, so the full maturity wall and the first operational break in the funding are not established; severity is medium, and a facility-level maturity profile would close it.

Several lines are printed as a dash and are not read as zero: asset impairments for 2023 and 2024, redeemable non-controlling interest income for 2025, the investment gain for 2023, temporary equity at 2024, 2025 and September 2026, notes receivable proceeds for the nine months of 2025, and long-term debt issuance and contingent consideration for the nine months of 2026; severity is low. Lines that exist in one statement and not the other are shown as not supplied for the periods without them.
The interim cash flow statements are printed year to date only, so discrete second and third quarter flows are not stated and are not constructed; severity is low.
The October 2026 acquisition has no stated purchase price and the dividend payable on 20 November 2026 has no stated total, so no pro forma net debt is stated; severity is low.

The 2024 income statement and balance sheet are taken as revised from the 2025 annual report, so the 2024 net income first reported is not used, and the balance sheet at 31 December 2023 comes from the 2024 annual report because the 2025 annual report does not print it; severity is low.
Covenant levels are not stated, so headroom is not calculable; severity is high, and the executed credit agreement would close it.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Lithia's creditor risk lies in cash allocation more than in its franchised retail model: share repurchases of USD 960.9 million in 2025 and USD 624.5 million in the nine months to September 2026 both exceeded operating cash flow.

Aftersales and finance and insurance supply about two thirds of gross profit, which steadies earnings while new-vehicle margins fall, but the filings do not identify the controlling holders, the board's composition or the note guarantors, so protections around distributions cannot be tested.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-8
### Key findings

Lithia sells new and used vehicles through franchised stores in the United States, the United Kingdom and Canada, and earns most of its profit from service, parts and finance and insurance. New vehicles are 49.70% of 2025 revenue but 20.39% of gross profit, while aftersales and finance and insurance together are 66.82% of gross profit, and the nine months to September 2026 show the same shape at 67.52%. That mix means vehicle margin compression, which cut new-vehicle gross profit per unit from USD 2,943 to USD 2,699 in the nine months, is cushioned by a service and finance base that is less tied to new-vehicle cycles.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-3

The company is concentrated by country and by franchise relationship. The United States is 78.53% of 2025 revenue, the United Kingdom 18.37% and Canada 3.10%, five manufacturers account for 25% of sales, and each store operates under a manufacturer franchise that the manufacturer may end on a change of management or ownership without its consent. Mechanically, a change in who controls the company could therefore put franchises, and the cash flow behind the debt, at risk at the same time as a change-in-control trigger in the credit agreement and note indentures.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation CALC-4

Growth has come through purchases of stores funded by floor plan debt. The company bought a large group of stores in 2024 for USD 1.1 billion net of floor plan debt, 17 in 2025 for USD 751.0 million and nine businesses in the first nine months of 2026 for USD 264.8 million, with USD 1.17 billion of annualized revenue acquired in 2026 to date including an October purchase of four stores. Acquired inventory is financed with new floor plan borrowing, so debt rises by more than the cash paid, and the stores acquired in 2026 had added USD 277.9 million of revenue and USD 11.2 million of operating income by September.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_lad-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2024-12-31_lad-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_a2026q3exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2

Shareholder returns are the main financial-policy risk. Repurchases and dividends were 45.09% of cash deployed in 2025 and 56.28% in the nine months to September 2026, against the company's stated target of 40% to 50%, and in both periods repurchases exceeded operating cash flow, which was USD 356.7 million in 2025 and an outflow of USD 204.9 million in the nine months. The share count fell 17.80% between the end of 2024 and September 2026 while book equity was almost unchanged, so the capital returned was financed by borrowing, because reported operating cash flow did not cover it. The board added USD 500 million of repurchase authority in May 2026, leaving USD 535.4 million available.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against the allocation concern is that 2025 shareholder returns were 45.09% of cash deployed, inside the 40% to 50% target, that the share count fell 17.80% as a result, and that the company says it has funding for the next twelve months. It would lose if the nine-month figure of 56.28% became the pattern while operating cash flow stays negative, because each dollar of buyback would then add a dollar of floor plan, warehouse or revolver debt; a board decision to slow repurchases, or a restricted-payments limit in the executed credit agreement that is already close to binding, would change conviction in either direction, and neither document is supplied.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The group is an acquirer. It bought 56 stores in 2023, a far larger group in 2024 and 17 in 2025, selling 10 and 12 in the last two years, and in 2026 it has bought nine businesses in the nine months to September for USD 264.8 million of cash, with the announced annualized revenue of the stores acquired in each quarter at USD 425 million, USD 340 million and USD 150 million, plus USD 250 million for four stores in Memphis in October 2026. Two stores were sold in the third quarter with USD 115 million of annualized revenue, after three in the second quarter with USD 120 million. The October purchase is a subsequent event: neither its price nor its funding is stated, and it is not in any period figure.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Lithia's credit profile is adequate but weakening at the margin: leverage on the company's own measure is 3.07x and reported EBITDA covers cash interest paid only 2.79x, while buybacks funded by borrowing are the main threat to creditors.

Aftersales and finance income give earnings ballast, asset-matched funding limits the risk in the largest debt lines, and funding maturities now run to 2028 and beyond, but covenants, ratings and note guarantors are not established, so this is a limited view that rests on the company's own non-GAAP measures.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-21_a2026q3exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-6
### Key findings

Leverage on the company's own measure rose over the year and has eased only slightly. Net debt over trailing Adjusted EBITDA was 2.50x in March 2025, 2.63x in September 2025, 3.07x in March 2026, 3.17x in June 2026 and 3.07x in September 2026, because net debt rose USD 521.3 million, or 11.66%, over the year while trailing Adjusted EBITDA fell USD 74.7 million, or 4.39%. Pro forma net debt for the October 2026 acquisition and the dividend expected on 2026-11-20 is not established, because neither amount is stated.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-29_a2026q1exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 9; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_a2026q2exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_a2026q3exx99earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 11; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-1; calculation CALC-2; calculation CALC-3; calculation CALC-4; calculation CALC-5; calculation CALC-6; calculation CALC-7; calculation CALC-8

Earnings are stabilising but not yet growing. Adjusted EBITDA fell 9.03% year on year in the first quarter of 2026 and 1.72% in the second, then rose 1.26% in the third, while operating margin fell from 5.45% in 2023 to 4.15% in the nine months to September 2026 and selling, general and administrative expense rose from 63.01% to 69.95% of gross profit. The mechanism is operating leverage: new-vehicle profit per unit keeps falling and same-store revenue is down, so each point of lost gross profit falls through to EBITDA, and a further decline of the size seen in the past year would lift leverage on the company's measure to 3.21x with net debt unchanged.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against a weakening view is that the company's own leverage is flat since March 2026 at 3.07x, that the high point of 3.17x in June 2026 has already eased, that third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA rose 1.26% on the year, that net credit losses on managed receivables fell to USD 47.8 million in the nine months from USD 54.1 million, and that 95.24% of the added receivables and most floor plan debt is matched by assets. That case would win if trailing Adjusted EBITDA turned up toward the USD 1,701.9 million of a year ago while repurchases slowed to within operating cash flow. It would lose if used-vehicle values or borrowing-base availability fell, because the matched debt would then be repaid faster than the assets convert, or if the executed credit agreement shows distribution limits that are already close to binding. On governance, the company kept a lead independent director when the chief executive became chairman, which is a partial check on the combined role.

### Limitations

- No covenant levels, restricted-payments baskets, guarantors or ratings were supplied, which limits the view on distribution capacity and on how much of the USD 1,256.5 million of available credit is usable; the assessment of financial policy is therefore a view of behaviour, not of legal capacity.

- Leverage on the company's measure uses the company's non-GAAP net debt and Adjusted EBITDA, which exclude inventory-related and financing-operations debt and deduct floor plan and financing interest, so the 3.07x and 6.00x figures describe the corporate layer only and are not comparable with the full-perimeter ratios.

- The downside case applies the reported fall of 4.4% in trailing Adjusted EBITDA once more to unchanged net debt and is an anchored assumption, not a forecast, so the 3.21x outcome shows sensitivity and not a probable level.

- Interim statements are unaudited, and year-end 2025 trailing Adjusted EBITDA is not printed, so the path of leverage between December 2025 and March 2026 on the company's measure is not established.
### Strengths and weaknesses

The first strength is a profit base weighted to service and finance. Aftersales and finance and insurance supplied 67.52% of gross profit in the nine months to September 2026, so a fall in new-vehicle margin reduces earnings less than the vehicle mix alone would imply, which supports cash flow visibility and debt service through a vehicle-price cycle.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29

The second strength is funding that is matched and extended. Inventory of USD 6,624.3 million stands against floor plan notes of USD 6,566.8 million and net finance receivables of USD 5,578.6 million against USD 4,509.2 million of financing-operations debt, and facility maturities were pushed to 2031, 2029 and 2028 in 2026, so near-term refinancing pressure on the large lines is low.

The third strength is clean claims outside debt: pension plans were in surplus by USD 30.1 million at the end of 2025 and no off-balance-sheet arrangement is reported, so there is no hidden senior claim from pensions in the supplied evidence.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 46; calculation CALC-21

The first weakness is distributions that exceed operating cash flow. Buybacks of USD 960.9 million in 2025 and USD 624.5 million in the nine months to September 2026 were paid while operating cash flow was USD 356.7 million and an outflow of USD 204.9 million, which raises net debt and reduces headroom for the corporate layer's creditors.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_lad-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The second weakness is margin and growth. Operating margin fell to 4.15% and selling, general and administrative expense reached 69.95% of gross profit, while same-store revenue was 1.5% lower, so the earnings cushion over interest is narrowing and growth depends on acquisitions that add floor plan debt.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_lad-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation CALC-19

The third weakness is that protections cannot be verified. Covenants, guarantors, collateral by instrument, ratings and board holdings are not in the supplied documents, and the chief executive is also chairman from 2026-10-19, so the checks that normally limit debt-funded distributions cannot be tested.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); Business & governance (CP-1A)
